name: Jettison
summary: The universal uninstaller for Omarchy. Every app, every source — gone cleanly, with nothing left behind. And everything can be undone.

featured.headline: Uninstall anything. Leave nothing behind.
featured.tagline: The universal uninstaller for Omarchy. Every app from every source in one list — removed properly, leftovers and all. It can't break your system, and it can undo anything.
featured.new_line: New in 2.0: every app from every source · Leftover hunter · Undo anything · Tidy up

features.title: Every app. Every source. One list.
features.body: Arch packages, AUR apps, Flatpaks, AppImages, Omarchy web apps, terminal apps, themes, apps with their own installers and stray launcher entries — Jettison finds them all automatically, with icons, versions, sizes and install dates. Search everything, sort by size, filter by source.

features.title: Leftover hunter
features.body: Uninstalling an app usually leaves its settings, data and caches scattered around your home folder. Jettison tracks them down — in ~/.config, ~/.local/share, ~/.cache, Flatpak data and autostart — shows their sizes, and clears them in one click.

features.title: Undo anything
features.body: Nothing goes into oblivion. Files land in the real Trash and Recently removed puts them back with one click — apps are reinstalled from the exact place they came from.

features.title: Can't break Omarchy
features.body: Everything Omarchy needs to start — Hyprland, the kernel, the login screen, sound, network — is Protected and can't be selected. If another app still needs something, Jettison tells you before anything happens.

features.title: Know exactly what goes
features.body: Every app gets its own page: what will be removed, which dependencies leave with it, how much space you get back, and the settings it keeps. No surprises.

features.title: Batch uninstall
features.body: Tick as many apps as you like and remove them all at once. One password, typed in a terminal you can see — Jettison never handles it. Apps in your home folder don't need a password at all.

features.title: Tidy up
features.body: Reclaim space Omarchy collects over time: unused dependencies, old package downloads (one copy stays so you can roll back), AUR build files, broken launcher entries and leftovers of apps you removed long ago.

features.title: Uninstall an open window
features.body: Not sure what an app is called? Click the target button, pick its window, and Jettison takes you straight to the app that owns it.

features.title: Dry run everything
features.body: See every step Jettison would take, in a terminal, without changing a thing.

features.title: Still removes a broken Omarchy Store
features.body: The original Jettison store remover is built in: it takes the Omarchy Store off cleanly even when it won't open, is stuck on a blank window or half-installed.

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Press GET in the Omarchy Store app, or run the one-line command above. Type your password when asked.

steps.title: Pick an app
steps.body: Open Jettison (Super + Space, type Jettison). Every app on your computer is already listed — search, or pick a source on the left.

steps.title: Press Uninstall
steps.body: Check what goes, press Uninstall, then choose which leftovers to clear. Changed your mind? Recently removed → Undo.

shortcuts.does: Search every app on this computer

faq.a: Arch packages, AUR apps, Flatpaks (yours or system-wide), AppImages, Omarchy web apps, terminal apps, Omarchy themes, apps with their own installers like SnapDock, stray launcher entries — and the Omarchy Store itself.

No. Everything Omarchy needs to start is Protected and can't be selected, and Jettison checks every removal with pacman first. If another app still needs something, or something essential would go with it, it stops and tells you why.

The settings, saved data and caches an app keeps in your home folder. Most uninstallers leave them behind. Jettison finds them by the app's own names and shows you each folder and its size before you clear it.

faq.q: I removed something by mistake. Can I get it back?
faq.a: Yes. Open Recently removed and press Undo. Files come back from Trash and apps are reinstalled from the same place they came from — as long as you haven't emptied the Trash.

faq.q: Why does it sometimes ask for my password?
faq.a: Removing system packages and system-wide Flatpaks needs it. It's typed in a terminal you can see, never into Jettison. Web apps, AppImages, terminal apps and themes are removed without a password.

faq.q: I had Jettison 1. What happened to the store remover?
faq.a: It's all still there, under Tools → Omarchy Store remover, and the old jettison --scan / --run commands still work. Removing Jettison itself afterwards is now off by default.

description:
Jettison is the universal uninstaller for Omarchy. Every app on your computer — wherever it came from — in one list, removed properly, with nothing left behind. And everything can be undone.

NEW IN 2.0
• Every source in one list: Arch packages, AUR, Flatpak, AppImages, Omarchy web apps, terminal apps, themes, self-installed apps and launcher entries
• Leftover hunter: clears the settings, data and caches apps leave in your home folder
• Undo anything: files go to Trash, apps are reinstalled from where they came from
• Tidy up: unused dependencies, old package downloads, AUR build files, broken launchers
• Uninstall an open window, batch uninstall, dry run

KNOWS EXACTLY WHAT GOES
Every app has its own page showing what will be removed, which dependencies leave with it, the space you get back and the settings it keeps.

CAN'T BREAK OMARCHY
Everything Omarchy needs to start — Hyprland, the kernel, the login screen, sound, network — is Protected. Jettison checks every removal with pacman first and stops if another app still needs something.

YOUR PASSWORD STAYS YOURS
System packages are removed in a terminal you can see; Jettison never handles your password. Web apps, AppImages, terminal apps and themes need no password at all.

STILL REMOVES A BROKEN OMARCHY STORE
The original Jettison store remover is built in under Tools — it works even when the store won't open.

COMMAND LINE
jettison list · jettison remove NAME · jettison leftovers NAME · jettison tidy · jettison history · jettison undo

Developed by Omarchy Development Labs. Free and open source (MIT).

DISCLAIMER
Jettison is provided as is, without warranty. It only removes what you select, keeps Omarchy's essentials protected, and moves home-folder files to Trash so they can be restored. The authors and the Omarchy Store accept no liability for data loss or damage. MIT licence.
